title: Amber Marshall Reveals the 1 Thing She Loves About Her Quiet Ranch Life
metaDescription: Amber Marshall, Heartland's Amy Fleming, has been married to photographer Shawn Turner since 2013. The pair share a quiet ranch life near Calgary.
author: EpisodeLens Staff
altText: Amber Marshall and Shawn Turner at their quiet ranch near Calgary with animals
html:
Amber Marshall has spent years playing Amy Fleming on Heartland, the long-running Canadian drama about a family that heals horses and, more often than not, heals itself. Off screen, her life looks a lot like the one fans imagine for her character: quiet, grounded, and surrounded by animals. She has been married to photographer Shawn Turner since July 27, 2013, and the two share a peaceful ranch life near Calgary.

Amber Marshall and the Heartland Role That Made Her a Fixture

For viewers who have followed Heartland since its early days, Amber Marshall is Amy Fleming. The show follows the Fleming family and their life at Heartland Ranch, a place where broken horses and broken people tend to find each other. Amy grows from a grieving teenager into a confident horse trainer, and Marshall has carried that arc through season after season.

That longevity is rare on television. Actors often cycle through a handful of roles in the time Marshall has spent in Amy's boots. She has become one of the most recognizable faces in Canadian television, and much of that recognition comes from the simple, steady way she plays a character who never chases the spotlight.

Inside Her Quiet Ranch Life with Shawn Turner

Marshall's real life echoes that same calm. She and Shawn Turner married on July 27, 2013, and they have built a life together near Calgary. The couple's ranch is home to a rotating cast of animals, and by all accounts it is the kind of place where the phone gets put down and the day moves at its own pace.

Turner works as a photographer, which means the two share a certain creative rhythm. One performs for the camera, the other captures what is in front of it. Their life together is not the stuff of tabloid drama. It is early mornings, feeding routines, and the kind of partnership that does not need a headline to feel real.

For Marshall, that quiet is not a retreat from her career. It is the thing that makes the career sustainable. Long-running shows demand stamina, and having a home base near Calgary, far from the noise of Hollywood, gives her somewhere to recharge between seasons.

Why Amber Marshall's Marriage Has Lasted

Marshall and Turner have been married since 2013, which in entertainment years is practically a lifetime. They keep their relationship largely private, rarely making it part of any public narrative. That choice seems deliberate. Marshall has never treated her marriage as content, and Turner has never positioned himself as a celebrity spouse.

What fans do see is a consistent picture: a couple who like being around animals, who value routine, and who seem genuinely content with a smaller world. In an industry that rewards visibility, that is its own kind of statement.

It also explains why Marshall has stayed so connected to Heartland's audience. She does not perform her off-screen life for them. She simply lives it, and lets them in just enough to see that Amy Fleming's world is not so far from her own.

What Keeps Fans Coming Back to Heartland

Heartland has built one of the most loyal audiences on television, and Marshall sits at the center of it. The show's fans are not casual viewers. They grew up with Amy, and many of them see Marshall as an extension of the character they love.

That bond is not something a publicist can manufacture. It comes from years of showing up, doing the work, and not burning the goodwill that comes with it. Marshall has done exactly that, and her life near Calgary reflects the same steady values the show has always championed.

For now, she seems happy to keep things simple: a marriage that has lasted since 2013, a ranch full of animals, and a role that still means something to millions of people. That is a rare combination, and Marshall does not appear to take any of it for granted.
